title: How Finely Can Vision-Language Models See Biology? Bio-VQA: A Benchmark for Taxonomic, Morphological, Spatial and Individual Reasoning

evidence.label: 明确提出新的评测资料或框架
evidence.excerpt: We present Bio-VQA, the largest biological visual question answering (VQA) benchmark and the only one to span four aspects of biological visual understanding: hierarchical taxonomic reasoning, fine-grained attribute grounding, quantitative spatial reasoning, and individual re-identification.

evidence.label: 描述任务、问题或评测环境
evidence.excerpt: In biodiversity monitoring, a single image raises several questions: which taxon, how many, which trait, and whether the individual has been seen before.

evidence.label: 描述评分指标或评测协议
evidence.excerpt: Bio-VQA contains 1.86M questions over 217K images from 11 public datasets, and extends right-or-wrong scoring to graded scoring, so a near-miss counts for more than a distant one.

evidence.label: 报告基线或多个模型的评测
evidence.excerpt: Evaluating 18 open-weight models from 3.75B to 38.4B parameters, we find that general visual capabilities do not transfer to biological organisms: the best model counts animals exactly on 41.7% of images with 2 to 10 individuals, less than half its accuracy on everyday objects at the same counts.

evidence.label: 给出任务规模或覆盖范围
